claude.sample_unit: patients with sepsis (9135 MIMIC-IV development; 3743 eICU-CRD external validation)

links.outcome: Prediction errors with versus without conformal prediction uncertainty estimates
links.effect: CP at mixed confidence reduced overall prediction errors by 27.6% (n=62) internally and 30.7% (n=412) externally; persistent ill errors 23.5% vs 41.5% internal, 31% vs 53.7% external.
links.quote: When the model was evaluated using a mixed confidence approach, with a confidence level of 85% for recovery and a confidence level of 75% for rapid death and persistent ill, the model with CP reduced overall prediction errors by 27.6% (n=62) and 30.7% (n=412) in the internal and external validation cohorts, respectively, compared with the model without CP ( Table 2 ).

links.outcome: Performance drop of AUROC from internal (MIMIC-IV) to external (eICU-CRD) validation
links.effect: Persistent ill AUROC fell from 0.807 to 0.696, recovery 0.843 to 0.764, rapid death 0.906 to 0.878; cohorts differed significantly in SOFA, admissions, mortality.
links.quote: In the external validation cohort, the mean AUROCs (SDs) were 0.878 (0.003) for rapid death, 0.764 (0.008) for recovery, and 0.696 (0.007) for persistent ill ( Multimedia Appendix 7 ).

links.effect: External AUROC (SD) was 0.878 rapid death, 0.764 recovery, and 0.696 persistent ill.
links.quote: In the external validation cohort, the mean AUROCs (SDs) were 0.878 (0.003) for rapid death, 0.764 (0.008) for recovery, and 0.696 (0.007) for persistent ill ( Multimedia Appendix 7 ).

links.effect: GBM had highest persistent-ill AUROC range, 0.806-0.807, versus NDF 0.779-0.802, RF 0.791-0.795, and LR 0.719-0.790.
links.quote: Of the 4 machine learning architectures in 3 model setups for predicting persistent ill on internal validation, GBM had the highest consistent performance of mean AUROC (SD) ranging from 0.806 (0.010) to 0.807 (0.010) compared to NDF ranging from 0.779 (0.013) to 0.802 (0.011), RF ranging from 0.791 (0.013) to 0.795 (0.010), and LR ranging from 0.719 (0.031) to 0.790 (0.007; Multimedia Appendix 6 ).

links.effect: Mixed-confidence CP reduced overall prediction errors by 27.6% (n=62) internal and 30.7% (n=412) external versus no CP.
links.quote: Compared to the model without CP, using the model with CP at a mixed confidence approach reduced overall prediction errors by 27.6% (n=62) and 30.7% (n=412) in the internal and external validation cohorts, respectively, as well as enabled the identification of more potentially persistent ill patients.

links.effect: Among uncertain {rapid death,persistent ill} outputs, persistent-ill cases were 46/62 (74.2%) internal and 351/496 (70.8%) external.
links.quote: Because among these predictions, 46 of 62 (74.2%) predictions were persistent ill in the internal validation cohort, and 351 of 496 (70.8%) predictions were persistent ill in the external validation cohort ( Table 3 ).
